channel.title: Buckleson blog
channel.description: Guides on custom blockchains, asset tokenization, wallets and AI-agent security.

item.title: What Can Blockchain Do Beyond Payments and Crypto?
item.description: Blockchain does far more than payments. See 8 real use cases, from private identity proofs and shared processes to tokenized assets, and when a database wins.

item.title: Blockchain vs Database: When Do You Need a Blockchain?
item.description: Blockchain vs database: use a blockchain only when several parties write to one record and none of them trusts one owner. See the checklist and trade-offs.

item.title: What Is Compliance as Code on a Blockchain?
item.description: Compliance as code turns KYC checks, limits and approvals into rules that a blockchain runs before each transaction. See how it works and where it falls short.

item.title: What Is MEV and How Can a Wallet Protect Users?
item.description: MEV is the profit that bots take when they place trades around a pending swap. See how sandwich attacks work and how a wallet protects users from them.

item.title: MPC vs Multisig Wallets: Which Is Safer?
item.description: MPC wallets split one key into shares, and multisig wallets need several full keys. Neither is always safer. Compare theft risk, recovery, approvals and costs.

item.title: What Is Proof of Reserve for Tokenized Assets?
item.description: Proof of reserve shows that real assets back every token in circulation. See how it works, where it falls short and how to build it into a tokenized asset.

item.title: What Are Shadow AI Agents and How Do You Find Them?
item.description: Shadow AI agents are AI tools and scripts that staff connect to company data without approval. See how to find them, list them and put them behind one gateway.

item.title: How Do Signed Match Results Stop Cheating in Games?
item.description: A signed match result shows who reported a score and that nobody changed it. See which cheats it stops, which it cannot and how payouts on a blockchain use it.

item.title: Is Your AI System Prompt a Secret?
item.description: No. Users can often make an AI model repeat its system prompt. Learn why prompts leak, what never belongs in one and how to enforce rules outside the model.

item.title: What Are Tokenized Bonds and How Do They Work?
item.description: Tokenized bonds are bonds recorded as tokens on a blockchain. See how issuance, coupons, transfer rules, trades and redemption work, and what stays the same.

item.title: Tokenized Deposits vs Stablecoins: What Is the Difference?
item.description: Tokenized deposits are bank money on a blockchain. Stablecoins are tokens backed by a reserve. Compare who issues them, who can hold them and how they settle.

item.title: How Can You Verify a Customer Without Seeing Their Data?
item.description: You can verify a customer without seeing their data. One trusted party checks the documents once, and others check a signed result or a proof of one fact.

item.title: How Do You Design a Web3 Game Economy With Tokens?
item.description: Web3 game economy design balances faucets that create tokens with sinks that remove them. Learn to set fair rewards, prove payouts and test before launch.

item.title: What Is a Blockchain Bridge and How Do You Make One Safe?
item.description: A blockchain bridge moves value between chains. See how lock and mint works, why bridges attract attackers and what a safe bridge checks before any release.

item.title: Why Do AI Agents Act on Hallucinations?
item.description: An AI agent hallucination becomes an incident when the agent acts on it. Learn the claim, check, act pattern that stops a false claim before it does harm.

item.title: What Is AI Agent Identity and Why Does It Matter?
item.description: AI agent identity gives each agent its own keys, rights and status. Learn why shared accounts fail and how short-lived tokens and signed identities stop abuse.

item.title: How Does an AI Agent Kill Switch Work?
item.description: An AI agent kill switch stops a rogue agent from outside its runtime. Learn how graduated containment, out-of-band stops and tamper-evident records work.

item.title: What Is AI Agent Memory Poisoning?
item.description: AI agent memory poisoning plants false facts or hidden orders in what an agent remembers. See how it spreads, how to protect memory writes and how to recover.

item.title: AI Agent Tool Calling: How to Secure Every Function Call
item.description: Tool calling lets AI agents act, and lets attackers act through them. Protect every call with allow-lists, argument checks, least privilege and egress rules.

item.title: What Is an AI Bill of Materials (AI-BOM)?
item.description: An AI bill of materials lists every model, dataset, package, MCP server and skill that your agents use. Learn how to pin, check and gate each part.

item.title: Asset Tokenization: How to Launch Tokenized Real-World Assets
item.description: A plain guide: what asset tokenization is, the five steps to launch tokenized gold, funds, invoices or property, and how compliance and settlement work.

item.title: Blockchain Data Encryption: The Four Layers That Matter
item.description: Blockchain data encryption in four layers: in transit, in use, on the ledger and at rest. What each layer protects against, and how Hyper 0X applies all four.

item.title: Blockchain Finality Explained: When Is a Payment Final?
item.description: Blockchain finality explained: probabilistic vs deterministic finality, what a reorg is, and why payments and settlement need transactions final in one pass.

item.title: Blockchain Payments for Merchants: How to Accept Them
item.description: How merchants can accept blockchain payments: checkout flow, settlement and finality, stablecoins versus volatile coins, fees, refunds and compliance basics.

item.title: Custodial vs Non-Custodial Wallets: Which to Offer?
item.description: A custodial wallet holds keys for the user. A non-custodial wallet keeps them on the device. Compare licensing, recovery and UX to pick the right model.

item.title: What Is Denial of Wallet and How Do You Stop It?
item.description: A denial of wallet attack makes an AI agent burn tokens until your budget is gone. Learn how token caps, loop detection and a compact context stop it.

item.title: How Blockchain Makes Esports Predictions Transparent
item.description: Blockchain can make esports predictions transparent with signed results, smart-contract payouts and a public record. See how it works and the legal limits.

item.title: How to Choose a Blockchain Development Company
item.description: What a blockchain development company must deliver, the questions to ask before you hire one, and the red flags that signal a costly rebuild later.

item.title: Layer 1 vs Layer 2 Blockchain: What Is the Difference?
item.description: Layer 1 vs layer 2 blockchain explained: the L1 protects and settles, the L2 runs transactions on top. How rollups work and when one L1 with many L2s fits.

item.title: MCP Server Security Risks: How to Vet and Gate Servers
item.description: MCP servers give AI agents tools, and attackers a new way in. See the main MCP server security risks, from tool poisoning to token theft, and how to vet them.

item.title: Why Do Multi-Agent AI Systems Fail in Cascades?
item.description: Multi-agent AI security starts at the hand-offs. See how one wrong fact spreads through a chain of agents, and how signed messages and circuit breakers stop it.

item.title: How Does a Multi-Chain Crypto Wallet Work?
item.description: One multi-chain crypto wallet can run Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Tron, TON, XRP, Stellar and Sui. How keys, addresses, swaps and bridges work, and the risks.

item.title: Permissioned vs Permissionless Blockchain: What Banks Need
item.description: Permissioned vs permissionless blockchain: why banks and regulated fintechs need known validators, private data and compliance, and when public chains fit.

item.title: Play-to-Earn Games Explained: What Broke and What Works
item.description: Play-to-earn games reward players with crypto for playing. See why early P2E economies collapsed and what a sustainable, skill-based model looks like.

item.title: How to Stop LLM Data Leaks: PII Redaction for AI Agents
item.description: Customer data and secrets leak into LLM prompts, logs and outputs. See how PII redaction, output filters and data residency stop leaks, with a GDPR view.

item.title: Tokenized Gold Explained: Backing, Audits and ETFs
item.description: Tokenized gold is a blockchain token that represents real gold in a vault. See how backing and audits work, and how it compares with gold ETFs and bullion.

item.title: Web3 Gaming Wallets: How Players Skip Seed Phrases
item.description: How web3 games give players wallets without seed phrases: embedded wallets through SDKs, passkeys, sponsored fees and session keys, and what players really own.

item.title: What Is a Wallet SDK and What Must It Include?
item.description: A wallet SDK lets a fintech add crypto wallets to its own app without building keys, chains and swaps. What a good SDK includes and how to integrate one.

item.title: What Is Micro-Investing? Round-Ups and Payment Slices
item.description: Micro-investing puts small, automatic amounts into assets through round-ups or a slice of every payment. See how it works, its pros and cons and who it suits.

item.title: What Is Prompt Injection? Examples and How to Stop It
item.description: Prompt injection hides instructions in text that an AI agent reads. See direct and indirect attacks, real examples and the layered defences that stop them.

item.title: Account Abstraction: Blockchain Without Seed Phrases
item.description: What account abstraction is and why it matters. Users sign in with a face scan and need no gas tokens. Limits and recovery after a lost phone are built in.

item.title: Dynamic Blocks: Fast When Quiet, No Backlog at Peaks
item.description: Dynamic blocks explained: fixed-size blocks build backlogs on busy days. Hyper 0X lets each L2 grow and shrink its blocks with demand, so payments never queue.

item.title: Private L2 vs Public Blockchain: Which Should an Enterprise Use?
item.description: Public blockchain, private chain or a private L2? Compare privacy, control, finality, cost and interoperability to pick the right option for your business.

item.title: Proof of Execution: Turning AI from a Black Box into a Record
item.description: Traditional logs cannot prove what an AI actually did. Signed, chained receipts on a blockchain give compliance, billing and disputes one verifiable record.

item.title: How to Launch Your Own Crypto Wallet: Build vs White-Label
item.description: Can a bank or fintech build a crypto wallet from scratch, or is a white-label wallet SDK the better path? Features, security, costs and timelines compared.

item.title: Atomic Settlement: Both Legs or Neither
item.description: What atomic settlement is and why Herstatt risk still matters. Hyper Wallet runs an order book inside Hyper 0X consensus to settle every trade in one step.

item.title: How to Secure AI Agents: 8 Attacks and How to Stop Them
item.description: AI agents need deep access to be useful. Learn the eight attacks that target them, from prompt injection to log tampering, and how to stop each one.

item.title: What Makes a Blockchain Post-Quantum-Resistant?
item.description: Harvest now, decrypt later is a real threat for records that must stay private for decades. How hybrid ML-KEM-768 + X25519 key exchange protects a blockchain.
